claim: A high throughput screening assay was used to screen approximately 170,000 compounds for splicing inhibition activity.
source: Using an automated setup, we screened ~170,000 compounds at a concentration of 50 µM for splicing inhibition activity.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of compounds screened and the method used.

claim: 30 compounds were reproducibly positive in the initial screen.
source: 30 reproducibly-positive compounds were further tested in standard in vitro splicing assays.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the number of reproducibly positive compounds.

claim: Eight compounds were confirmed to inhibit splicing of 32P-labelled MINX pre-mRNA in HeLa nuclear extract.
source: Eight compounds were confirmed to inhibit the splicing of 32P-labelled MINX pre-mRNA in HeLa nuclear extract.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of confirmed inhibitors.

claim: Compound 028 (cp028) has the chemical name 1-(2-Ethylphenyl)−5-((5-(4-fluorophenyl)furan-2-yl)methylene) pyrimidine-2,4,6 (1H,3H,5H)−trione.
source: Here we have focused on one of them, denoted compound 028 (cp028) 1-(2-Ethylphenyl)−5-((5-(4-fluorophenyl)furan-2-yl)methylene) pyrimidine-2,4,6 (1H,3H,5H)−trione (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript provides the chemical name and refers to Figure 1A showing the structure.

claim: In the presence of 50 µM cp028, splicing of MINX pre-mRNA in HeLa nuclear extract was reduced relative to the DMSO control after 60 min.
source: In the presence of 50 µM cp028, splicing of MINX pre-mRNA in HeLa nuclear extract was reduced relative to the DMSO control (that is, the cp028 solvent) after 60 min, with splicing completely abolished at concentrations above 150 µM (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript states the observation and refers to Figure 1B showing the data.

claim: Splicing was completely abolished at cp028 concentrations above 150 µM.
source: In the presence of 50 µM cp028, splicing of MINX pre-mRNA in HeLa nuclear extract was reduced relative to the DMSO control (that is, the cp028 solvent) after 60 min, with splicing completely abolished at concentrations above 150 µM (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the concentration at which splicing is completely abolished.

claim: The IC50 value of cp028 for inhibiting mRNA formation is 54 ± 4 µM.
source: A fine titration of cp028 revealed an IC50 value (where mRNA formation is inhibited by 50%) of 54 ± 4 µM (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript provides the IC50 value with error and refers to supporting figure.

claim: At inhibitory cp028 concentrations, an accumulation of spliceosomal complexes that run similar to A and B was observed.
source: At inhibitory cp028 concentrations, an accumulation of spliceosomal complexes that run similar to A and B were observed (Figure 1C).
evidence: The manuscript states the observation and refers to Figure 1C.

claim: In the presence of cp028, the amount of spliceosomal complexes peaks after 20 min.
source: A kinetic analysis of splicing complex formation revealed that in the presence of cp028, the amount of these complexes peaks already after 20 min (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript states the timing of peak complex formation.

claim: cp028 inhibits the A to B complex transition in higher eukaryotes.
source: Thus, in higher eukaryotes cp028 inhibits the A to B complex transition, and also the transition of the B complex to later spliceosomal complexes.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the effect of cp028 on spliceosome assembly.

claim: cp028 inhibits the transition of the B complex to later spliceosomal complexes.
source: Thus, in higher eukaryotes cp028 inhibits the A to B complex transition, and also the transition of the B complex to later spliceosomal complexes.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the effect of cp028 on spliceosome assembly.

claim: Similar results were obtained with an IgM pre-mRNA substrate.
source: Similar results were obtained with an IgM pre-mRNA substrate (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), indicating a general inhibitory effect of cp028 on pre-mRNA splicing in vitro.
evidence: The manuscript states that similar results were obtained with a different substrate.

claim: cp028 has a general inhibitory effect on pre-mRNA splicing in vitro.
source: Similar results were obtained with an IgM pre-mRNA substrate (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), indicating a general inhibitory effect of cp028 on pre-mRNA splicing in vitro.
evidence: The manuscript infers a general effect based on results with multiple substrates.

claim: cp028 did not inhibit splicing of actin pre-mRNA in S. cerevisiae whole cell extracts at a concentration up to 250 µM.
source: Interestingly, cp028 did not inhibit splicing of actin pre-mRNA in S. cerevisiae whole cell extracts at a concentration up to 250 µM (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that it targets or interferes with one or more spliceosomal component specifically involved in splicing in higher eukaryotes, and further that it does not inhibit splicing in a non-discriminatory manner.
evidence: The manuscript states the lack of inhibition in yeast extracts.

claim: cp028 targets or interferes with one or more spliceosomal components specifically involved in splicing in higher eukaryotes.
source: Interestingly, cp028 did not inhibit splicing of actin pre-mRNA in S. cerevisiae whole cell extracts at a concentration up to 250 µM (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that it targets or interferes with one or more spliceosomal component specifically involved in splicing in higher eukaryotes, and further that it does not inhibit splicing in a non-discriminatory manner.
evidence: The manuscript infers specificity based on the lack of effect in yeast.

claim: cp028 does not inhibit splicing in a non-discriminatory manner.
source: Interestingly, cp028 did not inhibit splicing of actin pre-mRNA in S. cerevisiae whole cell extracts at a concentration up to 250 µM (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that it targets or interferes with one or more spliceosomal component specifically involved in splicing in higher eukaryotes, and further that it does not inhibit splicing in a non-discriminatory manner.
evidence: The manuscript infers specificity of action based on species-specific effects.

claim: Spliceosomes assembled in the presence of cp028 migrated in two main peaks (I and II) of the glycerol gradient.
source: Spliceosomes assembled in the presence of cp028 migrated in two main peaks (I and II) of the gradient, which were each shifted to slightly lower S-values compared to the corresponding main peaks of the 4 min DMSO control reaction, which contain A and B complexes, respectively (Figure 1D).
evidence: The manuscript describes the gradient sedimentation results.

claim: Spliceosomes from peak I contained stoichiometric amounts of U1 and U2 snRNAs, plus the MINX-MS2 pre-mRNA.
source: Spliceosomes affinity-purified from peak I contained stoichiometric amounts of U1 and U2 snRNAs, plus the MINX-MS2 pre-mRNA (Figure 1E), indicating that they are spliceosomal A complexes.
evidence: The manuscript describes the RNA composition of peak I complexes.

claim: Complexes from peak I are spliceosomal A complexes.
source: Spliceosomes affinity-purified from peak I contained stoichiometric amounts of U1 and U2 snRNAs, plus the MINX-MS2 pre-mRNA (Figure 1E), indicating that they are spliceosomal A complexes.
evidence: The manuscript infers the identity of the complexes based on RNA composition.

claim: A028 complexes are designated as spliceosomal A complexes stalled in the presence of cp028.
source: Mass spectrometry (MS) analyses of these complexes, designated A028, revealed primarily U1 and U2 snRNP proteins, with only a few differences in other splicing factors compared to 'kinetic' A complexes, purified after splicing for 4 min (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly names the complexes A028.

claim: A028 complexes contain primarily U1 and U2 snRNP proteins.
source: Mass spectrometry (MS) analyses of these complexes, designated A028, revealed primarily U1 and U2 snRNP proteins, with only a few differences in other splicing factors compared to 'kinetic' A complexes, purified after splicing for 4 min (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes the protein composition based on MS analysis.

claim: Abundant proteins in the A028 complex include essentially all U1 and U2 snRNP proteins, plus U2AF65, U2AF35, SRSF1, SRSF7, hnRNPA1, and SPF30.
source: Abundant proteins (with a molecular mass above 25 kDa) in the A028 complex included essentially all U1 and U2 snRNP proteins, plus U2AF65, U2AF35, SRSF1, SRSF7, hnRNPA1, and SPF30 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript lists abundant proteins identified by 2D gel electrophoresis and MS.

claim: A028 is very similar to A complexes formed in the absence of inhibitor.
source: A nearly identical set of abundant/moderately-abundant proteins is found in kinetically-stalled A complexes (Agafonov et al., 2011), indicating that A028 is very similar to A complexes formed in the absence of inhibitor.
evidence: The manuscript compares A028 to previously characterized A complexes.

claim: cp028 has only a moderate effect on tri-snRNP stability, with most tri-snRNPs still intact under splicing conditions.
source: Thus, cp028 has only a moderate affect on tri-snRNP stability, with most tri-snRNPs still intact under splicing conditions.
evidence: The manuscript concludes based on gradient centrifugation and immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Affinity-purified complexes from gradient peak II contained stoichiometric amounts of U2, U5, U6 snRNA and the MINX-MS2 pre-mRNA, but substantially reduced levels of both U1 and U4 snRNAs.
source: Affinity-purified complexes formed in the presence of cp028, that were isolated from gradient peak II, contained stoichiometric amounts of U2, U5, U6 snRNA and the MINX-MS2 pre-mRNA, but substantially reduced levels of both U1 and U4 snRNAs (Figure 1E), suggesting that they are stalled at the Bact stage after Brr2-mediated dissociation of U4 snRNA.
evidence: The manuscript describes the RNA composition of peak II complexes.

claim: The B-like complex that accumulates in the presence of cp028 is designated B028.
source: The B-like complex that accumulates in the presence of cp028 (henceforth designated B028) has, in contrast, a lower S-value than B and also migrates faster than a Bact complex on a native gel, suggesting that it is a novel assembly intermediate.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly names the complex B028.

claim: B028 has a lower S-value than B complexes.
source: The B-like complex that accumulates in the presence of cp028 (henceforth designated B028) has, in contrast, a lower S-value than B and also migrates faster than a Bact complex on a native gel, suggesting that it is a novel assembly intermediate.
evidence: The manuscript describes the sedimentation behavior of B028.

claim: B028 migrates faster than a Bact complex on a native gel.
source: The B-like complex that accumulates in the presence of cp028 (henceforth designated B028) has, in contrast, a lower S-value than B and also migrates faster than a Bact complex on a native gel, suggesting that it is a novel assembly intermediate.
evidence: The manuscript describes the migration behavior of B028 on native gels.

claim: B028 is a novel assembly intermediate.
source: The B-like complex that accumulates in the presence of cp028 (henceforth designated B028) has, in contrast, a lower S-value than B and also migrates faster than a Bact complex on a native gel, suggesting that it is a novel assembly intermediate.
evidence: The manuscript infers that B028 is a novel intermediate based on its distinct properties.

claim: B028 complexes contain predominantly U2 and U5 snRNP proteins.
source: MS analysis (Supplementary file 1) and 2D gel electrophoresis followed by MS (Figure 2A,B) revealed that B028 complexes, like B complexes, contain predominantly U2 and U5 snRNP proteins, as well as most proteins from the group designated B-specific (RED, MFAP1, hSmu-1, hPrp38, hSnu23, NPW38 and NPW38BP) that are recruited at the B complex stage and are no longer abundant/present in the mature human Bact complex (Bessonov et al., 2010; Agafonov et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript describes the protein composition based on MS and 2D gel analysis.

claim: B028 complexes contain most B-specific proteins (RED, MFAP1, hSmu-1, hPrp38, hSnu23, NPW38 and NPW38BP).
source: MS analysis (Supplementary file 1) and 2D gel electrophoresis followed by MS (Figure 2A,B) revealed that B028 complexes, like B complexes, contain predominantly U2 and U5 snRNP proteins, as well as most proteins from the group designated B-specific (RED, MFAP1, hSmu-1, hPrp38, hSnu23, NPW38 and NPW38BP) that are recruited at the B complex stage and are no longer abundant/present in the mature human Bact complex (Bessonov et al., 2010; Agafonov et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript lists B-specific proteins found in B028.

claim: U4/U6 proteins such as Prp3, Prp4 and Prp31 are present in very low amounts in B028.
source: U4/U6 proteins, such as Prp3, Prp4 and Prp31, are present in very low amounts in B028, consistent with loss of the U4 snRNA (Supplementary file 1, Figure 2).
evidence: The manuscript describes the low abundance of U4/U6 proteins in B028.

claim: Only minor amounts of the tri-snRNP-specific proteins hSnu66 (110K) and hSAD1 (65K) are detected in B028.
source: In addition, only minor amounts of the tri-snRNP-specific proteins hSnu66 (110K) and hSAD1 (65K) are detected in B028.
evidence: The manuscript states the low abundance of tri-snRNP proteins in B028.

claim: The U6-associated Lsm 2–8 proteins are still abundant in B028.
source: In contrast, the U6-associated Lsm 2–8 proteins, which like the U4/U6 and tri-snRNP-specific proteins are normally lost during the conversion of B to Bact, are still abundant based on the total spectral counts of peptides sequenced by MS (Supplementary file 1) and also on immunoblotting with antibodies against the Lsm4 protein (Figure 2C).
evidence: The manuscript describes the abundance of Lsm proteins in B028 based on MS and western blotting.

claim: Bact-specific proteins are absent or highly underrepresented in B028.
source: Bact-specific proteins, which are only abundant in the Bact complex but not in C, and Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins, as well as other Bact proteins, which are recruited or more stably associated in Bact complexes (Bessonov et al., 2010; Agafonov et al., 2011), are absent or highly underrepresented in B028.
evidence: The manuscript states the absence or low abundance of Bact-specific proteins in B028.

claim: Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins are absent or highly underrepresented in B028.
source: Bact-specific proteins, which are only abundant in the Bact complex but not in C, and Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins, as well as other Bact proteins, which are recruited or more stably associated in Bact complexes (Bessonov et al., 2010; Agafonov et al., 2011), are absent or highly underrepresented in B028.
evidence: The manuscript states the absence or low abundance of Prp19/CDC5L complex proteins in B028.

claim: SF3b155 is hyperphosphorylated during catalytic activation of the spliceosome.
source: The U2 snRNP SF3b155 protein is hyperphosphorylated during catalytic activation of the spliceosome (Wang et al., 1998; Girard et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies showing SF3b155 hyperphosphorylation.

claim: SF3b155 is not hyperphosphorylated in B028 complexes.
source: Immunoblotting with anti-SF3b155 antibodies that recognize both non-phosphorylated SF3b155 and its slower-migrating, hyperphosphorylated form, as well as with an antibody specific for phosphorylated SF3b155, demonstrated that SF3b155 is not hyperphosphorylated in B028 complexes (Figure 2C).
evidence: The manuscript describes western blotting results showing lack of SF3b155 hyperphosphorylation in B028.

claim: B028 complexes are stalled at an intermediate stage between B and Bact.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that B028 complexes are stalled at an intermediate stage between B and Bact, after displacement of U4 snRNA by Brr2 and loss of the U4/U6-specific proteins, but before release of the B-specific and Lsm proteins, and recruitment/stable integration of Bact-specific and Prp19/CDC5L proteins.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes the compositional analysis to conclude B028 is an intermediate.

claim: The large exchange of proteins during the B to Bact transition occurs stepwise.
source: Assuming that the B028 complex does not represent an atypical assembly intermediate, these data indicate that the large exchange of proteins during the B to Bact transition occurs stepwise, with the release of U4/U6 proteins occurring prior to and independently of the exchange other spliceosomal proteins (see Discussion).
evidence: The manuscript infers stepwise protein exchange based on B028 composition.

claim: The release of U4/U6 proteins occurs prior to and independently of the exchange of other spliceosomal proteins during the B to Bact transition.
source: Assuming that the B028 complex does not represent an atypical assembly intermediate, these data indicate that the large exchange of proteins during the B to Bact transition occurs stepwise, with the release of U4/U6 proteins occurring prior to and independently of the exchange other spliceosomal proteins (see Discussion).
evidence: The manuscript infers the order of protein release based on B028 composition.

claim: U2/U6 helix II is formed in B, B028, and Bact complexes.
source: A U2/U6 crosslink, which based on its migration behaviour is U2/U6 helix II (Anokhina et al., 2013), was detected in all complexes, albeit less efficiently in B and B028, indicating base pairing between the 5' and 3' end of U2 and U6, respectively.
evidence: The manuscript describes psoralen crosslinking results indicating U2/U6 helix II formation.

claim: A U6/pre-mRNA crosslink consistent with U6 ACAGA box/5'SS base pairing interaction was detected in B, B028, and Bact complexes.
source: Likewise, a U6/pre-mRNA crosslink, consistent with a U6 ACAGA box/5'SS base pairing interaction, was also detected in all three complexes, but less efficiently in B028 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes psoralen crosslinking results indicating U6/5'SS interaction.

claim: U2/U6 helix II appears to be formed in all complexes based on the lack of chemical modification of U2 nts 3–11 and U6 nts 88–95.
source: Consistent with our psoralen crosslinking results, U2/U6 helix II appears to be formed in all complexes, based on the lack of chemical modification of U2 nts 3–11 and U6 nts 88–95 (which form helix II), as evidenced by the absence of RT stops above background at these nucleotides (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript describes chemical modification results supporting U2/U6 helix II formation.

claim: Chemical modification supported the formation of the base pairing interaction between the U6 ACAGA box (nts A40-A44) and intron nucleotides near the 5'SS in B028.
source: Chemical modification also supported the formation of the base pairing interaction between the U6 ACAGA box (nts A40-A44) and intron nucleotides near the 5'SS in B028. That is, U6 nts A40-A44, as well as PM5-10 intron nts + 4 to +8 (relative to the 5'SS) were protected from modification in purified B028 and Bact complexes (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript describes chemical modification results supporting U6/5'SS interaction.

claim: U2 nucleotides that base pair with the BPS (G33-A38), with the exception of U2-G33, were not modified in B028 or Bact.
source: U2 nucleotides that base pair with the BPS (G33-A38), with the exception of U2-G33, were also not modified in B028 or Bact, consistent with the formation of the U2/BPS helix.
evidence: The manuscript describes chemical modification results supporting U2/BPS helix formation.

claim: Human U2 helix IIc is not formed in B028 complexes, nor in Bact.
source: However, human U2 nts A88-A95 and U53-U60, which would be base paired if helix IIc were formed, are accessible in B028 and Bact complexes, suggesting that U2 helix IIc is not formed in B028 complexes, nor in Bact, as previously shown (Anokhina et al., 2013) (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript describes chemical modification results indicating U2 helix IIc is not formed.

claim: The U6 ISL is formed in B028 and Bact complexes.
source: Most nucleotides comprising the U6 ISL loop (G67-A70) are accessible in Bact, whereas nucleotides forming the stem (U57-U64 and A70-A77) are not accessible or only very weakly accessible (with the exception of A70 and G75), consistent with the formation of the ISL (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript describes chemical modification results supporting U6 ISL formation.

claim: U6 nts 79–81 are protected in B028, but not in Bact.
source: Interestingly, U6 nts 79–81 are protected in B028, but not in Bact, suggesting that the lower part of the ISL stem is extended in B028 (Figure 3), consistent with the formation of a four-way U2-U6 junction (Figure 3), in contrast to the three-way junction that forms in Bact.
evidence: The manuscript describes chemical modification results showing differential protection of U6 nts 79-81.

claim: The lower part of the ISL stem is extended in B028.
source: Interestingly, U6 nts 79–81 are protected in B028, but not in Bact, suggesting that the lower part of the ISL stem is extended in B028 (Figure 3), consistent with the formation of a four-way U2-U6 junction (Figure 3), in contrast to the three-way junction that forms in Bact.
evidence: The manuscript infers ISL stem extension based on chemical modification data.

claim: The conformation of the U2/U6 junction in B028 differs from that in Bact, possibly forming a four-way as opposed to a three-way junction.
source: Taken together, our results indicate that the U6 ISL and U2/U6 helix Ia are formed in B028, but that the conformation of the U2/U6 junction in B028 differs from that in Bact, possibly forming a four-way as opposed to a three-way junction.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes chemical modification data to infer different U2/U6 junction conformations.

claim: The catalytic RNA network of the spliceosome is rearranged in multiple steps during catalytic activation.
source: This, in turn, is consistent with the idea that the catalytic RNA network of the spliceosome is rearranged in multiple steps during catalytic activation.
evidence: The manuscript infers stepwise RNA rearrangement based on the different U2/U6 conformations in B028 vs Bact.

claim: Purified B028 can be chased into a mature spliceosome that catalyzes both steps of splicing.
source: However, when micrococcal nuclease (MN) treated nuclear extract—in which all endogenous snRNPs were degraded—was added, both catalytic steps of splicing were observed, at levels similar to that observed with purified B complexes plus MN-treated extract (Figure 4). Splicing was not observed when pre-mRNA alone was incubated under splicing conditions with MN-treated extract (Figure 4). Thus, purified B028 can be chased into a mature spliceosome that catalyzes both steps of splicing, demonstrating that it is a functional intermediate.
evidence: The manuscript describes chase experiments showing B028 can complete splicing.

claim: B028 is a functional intermediate.
source: Thus, purified B028 can be chased into a mature spliceosome that catalyzes both steps of splicing, demonstrating that it is a functional intermediate.
evidence: The manuscript concludes B028 is functional based on chase experiments.

claim: When cp028 was added to the MN-treated extract, no splicing was observed after incubation with both B and B028 complexes.
source: However, when cp028 was added to the MN-treated extract, no splicing was observed after incubation with both B and B028 complexes (Figure 4).
evidence: The manuscript describes the effect of adding cp028 to chase reactions.

claim: cp028 binds to and/or inactivates a splicing factor required for the conversion of the B/B028 complexes into catalytically active spliceosomes.
source: This suggests that cp028 binds to and/or inactivates a splicing factor required for the conversion of the B/B028 complexes into catalytically active spliceosomes.
evidence: The manuscript infers the mechanism of cp028 action based on chase experiment results.

claim: The majority of B028 particles exhibit a roughly triangular shape, with a lower foot-like protrusion.
source: The majority of B028 particles exhibit a roughly triangular shape, with a lower foot-like protrusion.
evidence: The manuscript describes the morphology of B028 observed by EM.

claim: In the most dominant classes (comprising ca. 40%), the B028 complex exhibits a triangular shape with a long density element on the left and an upper more globular domain.
source: Classification and class averaging of these single particle images (Figure 5B) revealed that in the most dominant classes (comprising ca. 40%) the B028 complex exhibits a triangular shape with a long density element on the left and an upper more globular domain (Figure 5B, columns 1–2).
evidence: The manuscript describes the predominant EM class averages of B028.

claim: The basic morphology of the various EM views of the B028 complex indicates that it shares similarities with the spliceosomal B complex when the triangular views are considered.
source: The basic morphology of the various EM views of the B028 complex indicates that it shares similarities with the spliceosomal B complex, when the triangular views are considered, and similarities with the Bact complex, when the mushroom views are compared.
evidence: The manuscript compares B028 morphology to B and Bact complexes.

claim: The basic morphology of the various EM views of the B028 complex indicates that it shares similarities with the Bact complex when the mushroom views are compared.
source: The basic morphology of the various EM views of the B028 complex indicates that it shares similarities with the spliceosomal B complex, when the triangular views are considered, and similarities with the Bact complex, when the mushroom views are compared.
evidence: The manuscript compares B028 morphology to B and Bact complexes.

claim: There appear to be clear structural differences between B028 and B complexes.
source: Thus, despite many similarities, there appear to be clear structural differences between B028 and B complexes.
evidence: The manuscript concludes there are structural differences based on EM analysis.

claim: Replacing the fluorine of the p-fluorophenyl group with a phenyl group (analogue 343868) abolished inhibition activity completely.
source: Replacing the fluorine of the p-fluorophenyl group with a phenyl group (analogue 343868) or replacing the p-fluorophenyl group by a piperidine (analogue 344353) (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2) abolished inhibition activity completely.
evidence: The manuscript describes structure-activity relationship results.

claim: Replacing the p-fluorophenyl group by a piperidine (analogue 344353) abolished inhibition activity completely.
source: Replacing the fluorine of the p-fluorophenyl group with a phenyl group (analogue 343868) or replacing the p-fluorophenyl group by a piperidine (analogue 344353) (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2) abolished inhibition activity completely.
evidence: The manuscript describes structure-activity relationship results.

claim: Removing the furan group reduced the potency dramatically (analogues 343878 and 343879).
source: In addition, removing the furan group also reduced the potency dramatically (analogues 343878 and 343879).
evidence: The manuscript describes structure-activity relationship results.

claim: The fluorophenyl group and the furan group are required for inhibiting pre-mRNA splicing in vitro.
source: Thus, the fluorophenyl group and the furan group are required for inhibiting pre-mRNA splicing in vitro and likely play an important role in target recognition.
evidence: The manuscript concludes based on structure-activity relationship studies.

claim: The fluorophenyl group and the furan group likely play an important role in target recognition.
source: Thus, the fluorophenyl group and the furan group are required for inhibiting pre-mRNA splicing in vitro and likely play an important role in target recognition.
evidence: The manuscript infers the role of these groups based on structure-activity relationship studies.

claim: Nearly all modifications in the ethylphenyl group had only minimal or no substantial effect on the potency of cp028.
source: Nearly all modifications in the ethylphenyl group (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2), or its omission (analogue 343135), had only minimal or no substantial effect on the potency of cp028, suggesting that this structural feature it is not essential for splicing inhibition in vitro.
evidence: The manuscript describes structure-activity relationship results.

claim: The ethylphenyl group is not essential for splicing inhibition in vitro.
source: Nearly all modifications in the ethylphenyl group (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2), or its omission (analogue 343135), had only minimal or no substantial effect on the potency of cp028, suggesting that this structural feature it is not essential for splicing inhibition in vitro.
evidence: The manuscript infers the ethylphenyl group is not essential based on structure-activity relationship studies.

claim: The ethylphenyl site could potentially be used to introduce a tag to identify the target(s) of compound 028 in the splicing reaction.
source: Thus, this site could potentially be used to introduce a tag to identify the target(s) of compound 028 in the splicing reaction.
evidence: The manuscript speculates on potential use of the ethylphenyl site for tagging.

claim: Reduction of the conjugated double bond (analogue 343139) completely abolished splicing inhibition.
source: Notably, reduction of the conjugated double bond (analogue 343139, Figure 6C) completely abolished splicing inhibition, suggesting that cp028 likely exerts its inhibitory activity by covalently modifying one or several target proteins and/or that the rotational freedom afforded by a single bond may be deleterious for its inhibition activity.
evidence: The manuscript describes structure-activity relationship results.

claim: cp028 likely exerts its inhibitory activity by covalently modifying one or several target proteins.
source: Notably, reduction of the conjugated double bond (analogue 343139, Figure 6C) completely abolished splicing inhibition, suggesting that cp028 likely exerts its inhibitory activity by covalently modifying one or several target proteins and/or that the rotational freedom afforded by a single bond may be deleterious for its inhibition activity.
evidence: The manuscript speculates on the mechanism of cp028 action based on structure-activity relationship.

claim: The rotational freedom afforded by a single bond may be deleterious for cp028's inhibition activity.
source: Notably, reduction of the conjugated double bond (analogue 343139, Figure 6C) completely abolished splicing inhibition, suggesting that cp028 likely exerts its inhibitory activity by covalently modifying one or several target proteins and/or that the rotational freedom afforded by a single bond may be deleterious for its inhibition activity.
evidence: The manuscript speculates on the importance of the double bond based on structure-activity relationship.

claim: cp028 represents a new tool to study pre-mRNA splicing mechanisms, in particular to dissect/modulate the highly complex spliceosome activation process.
source: Thus, cp028 represents a new tool to study pre-mRNA splicing mechanisms, in particular to dissect/modulate the highly complex spliceosome activation process.
evidence: The manuscript concludes on the utility of cp028 as a research tool.

claim: The loss of the U4/U6 proteins can occur independently of the release of the U6 Lsm proteins or B-specific proteins.
source: Our MS and 2D gel analyses of purified B028 complexes, together with western blotting, suggest that the loss of the U4/U6 proteins (hPrp3, hPrp4, hPrp31, 20K and 15.5K), presumably during the Brr2-mediated unwinding of the U4/U6 duplex, can occur independently of the release of the U6 Lsm proteins or B-specific proteins.
evidence: The manuscript infers independent protein release based on B028 composition.

claim: The recruitment of the human Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins, as well as Bact-specific proteins, appear to occur after the release of the U4/U6-specific proteins.
source: Likewise, the recruitment of the human Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins, as well as Bact-specific proteins, appear to occur after the release of the U4/U6-specific proteins.
evidence: The manuscript infers the order of protein recruitment based on B028 composition.

claim: The recruitment of the NTC occurs after release of the U4 snRNA.
source: A number of studies including very recent single molecule studies in yeast, indicate that the recruitment of the NTC occurs after release of the U4 snRNA (Tarn et al., 1993; Chan et al., 2003; Hoskins et al., 2016), which is consistent with U4/U6 protein release preceeding recruitment of the vast majority of the Prp19/CDC5L complex.
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies on NTC recruitment timing.

claim: The formation of a rearranged U6 structure, including formation of the U6 ISL, may provide new binding sites that enable the recruitment/stable binding of the Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins, and/or Bact proteins.
source: Release of the U6 snRNA from U4 allows rearrangements in the structure of the U6 snRNA. The formation of a rearranged U6 structure, including formation of the U6 ISL, may provide new binding sites that enable the recruitment/stable binding of the Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins, and/or Bact proteins.
evidence: The manuscript speculates on the role of U6 rearrangement in protein recruitment.

claim: In yeast, the NTC was reported to be required for the release of the Lsm proteins from the 3′-end of U6 snRNA.
source: In yeast, the NTC was reported to be required for the release of the Lsm proteins from the 3′-end of U6 snRNA (Chan et al., 2003), thus the interaction or stable association of the Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins with the spliceosome may be a prerequisite for the subsequent loss of the Lsm proteins from the spliceosome during activation.
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study on NTC role in Lsm protein release.

claim: The interaction or stable association of the Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins with the spliceosome may be a prerequisite for the subsequent loss of the Lsm proteins from the spliceosome during activation.
source: In yeast, the NTC was reported to be required for the release of the Lsm proteins from the 3′-end of U6 snRNA (Chan et al., 2003), thus the interaction or stable association of the Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins with the spliceosome may be a prerequisite for the subsequent loss of the Lsm proteins from the spliceosome during activation.
evidence: The manuscript infers a prerequisite relationship based on cited yeast studies.

claim: Several NTC proteins (e.g. Syf1, Syf2 and Syf3) are close to U2/U6 helix II in the S. cerevisiae spliceosomal Bact complex.
source: Indeed, recent cryo-EM studies of the S. cerevisiae spliceosomal Bact complex, revealed that several NTC proteins (e.g. Syf1, Syf2 and Syf3) are close to U2/U6 helix II and thus to the 3' end of the U6 snRNA (Rauhut et al., 2016; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript cites cryo-EM studies showing NTC protein locations.

claim: The binding of Lsm proteins and NTC proteins (Syf1, Syf2, Syf3) to the 3' end of U6 is likely mutually exclusive.
source: As the Lsm proteins bind the 3' end of U6 (Achsel et al., 1999), it is likely that their binding and that of the aforementioned NTC proteins is mutually exclusive.
evidence: The manuscript infers mutual exclusivity based on binding site proximity.

claim: Spliceosomal proteins promote the formation of a U2/U6 three-helix junction.
source: U2/U6 four-helix junction formation had been documented previously only with protein-free snRNAs (Sashital et al., 2004; Guo et al., 2009), and it is thus likely that spliceosomal proteins promote the formation of a U2/U6 three-helix junction.
evidence: The manuscript infers protein role in promoting three-helix junction based on previous in vitro studies.

claim: Subsequent conversion of the apparent U2/U6 four-way junction observed in B028, to a three-way junction, may require the interaction of proteins normally recruited/stabilized during activation, and/or the loss of the Lsm or B-specific proteins.
source: Subsequent conversion of the apparent U2/U6 four-way junction observed in B028, to a three-way junction, may require the interaction of proteins normally recruited/stabilized during activation, and/or the loss of the Lsm or B-specific proteins, that are normally released prior to Bact formation.
evidence: The manuscript speculates on requirements for U2/U6 junction conversion.

claim: In the yeast Bact complex, the catalytic U2/U6 RNA network is contacted by Prp8, Cef1 (CDC5L in human), Prp46 (Prl1 in human), Syf3, Prp45 (SKIP/SNW1 in human), and Cwc2 (RBM22 in human).
source: In the yeast Bact complex, the catalytic U2/U6 RNA network is contacted not only by the U5 Prp8 protein, but also by Cef1 (CDC5L in human) and Prp46 (Prl1 in human), which are present in the human Prp19/CDC5L complex, and the Prp19/CDC5L-related proteins Syf3, Prp45 (SKIP/SNW1 in human) and Cwc2 (RBM22 in human) (Rasche et al., 2012; Rauhut et al., 2016; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript cites structural studies showing protein-RNA contacts in yeast Bact.

claim: The Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins likely act as chaperones that help to form/maintain the active conformation of the RNA network.
source: Given the multiple contacts that the Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins make with the catalytic RNA network of the spliceosome already at the Bact stage, it is very likely that they act as chaperones that help to form/maintain the active conformation of the RNA network.
evidence: The manuscript infers a chaperone role based on protein-RNA contacts.

claim: Cwc2 helps to stabilize U2/U6 helix 1.
source: Indeed, genetic experiments in S. cerevisiae indicate that Cwc2 helps to stabilize U2/U6 helix 1 (Hogg et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites genetic experiments showing Cwc2 function.

claim: Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins may shift the equilibrium toward the U2/U6 three helix structure once they are stably incorporated into the spliceosome.
source: As the U2/U6 three and four helix conformations are competing structures, and B028 complexes lack the Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins, these proteins may shift the equilibrium toward the three helix structure once they are stably incorporated into the spliceosome.
evidence: The manuscript speculates on the role of Prp19/CDC5L complex in shifting RNA conformation equilibrium.

claim: cp028 may have multiple spliceosome-related targets.
source: While the target(s) of cp028 remain unclear, the fact that two different steps of the spliceosome assembly pathway are stalled, suggest that cp028 may have multiple spliceosome-related targets.
evidence: The manuscript speculates on multiple targets based on effects at multiple stages.

claim: Mammalian spliceosomes contain a large number of proteins not found in S. cerevisiae.
source: Indeed, while there is conservation of the core spliceosomal components between yeast and man, mammalian spliceosomes contain a large number of proteins not found in S. cerevisiae (Fabrizio et al., 2009).
evidence: The manuscript cites a study on spliceosome composition differences.

claim: The conversion of the spliceosomal A complex into a B complex with stably associated U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP is dependent on several splicing factors, including SPF30, 65K/hSAD1, 110K/hSART1, SR proteins, hPrp4K, SRPK2, and Prp28.
source: The conversion of the spliceosomal A complex into a B complex with stably associated U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP is dependent not only on an intact tri-snRNP, but also on several splicing factors, including SPF30 (Rappsilber et al., 2001; Meister et al., 2001), the U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP proteins 65K/hSAD1 and 110K/hSART1 (Makarova et al., 2001), SR proteins (Roscigno and Garcia-Blanco, 1995), the kinases hPrp4K (Schneider et al., 2010) and SRPK2 (Mathew et al., 2008) and the DEAD-box helicase Prp28 (Staley and Guthrie, 1999; Mathew et al., 2008; Boesler et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies on factors required for A to B transition.

claim: One or more of the factors required for A to B transition (SPF30, 65K/hSAD1, 110K/hSART1, SR proteins, hPrp4K, SRPK2, Prp28) are potentially targeted directly or indirectly by cp028.
source: Thus, one or more of these proteins are potentially targeted directly or indirectly by cp028.
evidence: The manuscript speculates on potential cp028 targets.

claim: cp028 may affect the structure or composition of the A complex such that stable tri-snRNP integration is impaired.
source: It is also conceivable that cp028 affects the structure or composition of the A complex such that stable tri-snRNP integration is impaired.
evidence: The manuscript speculates on an alternative mechanism of cp028 action.

claim: A028 no longer contained stoichiometric amounts of the DEAD box protein Prp5 and the splicing factor SPF45.
source: However, the protein composition of affinity-purified A028 complexes was nearly identical to that of A complexes formed in the absence of cp028, except A028 no longer contained stoichiometric amounts of the DEAD box protein Prp5 and the splicing factor SPF45, both of which are not involved in B complex formation (Ruby et al., 1993; Lallena et al., 2002; Liang and Cheng, 2015).
evidence: The manuscript describes differences in A028 composition compared to A complexes.

claim: Prp5 and SPF45 are not involved in B complex formation.
source: However, the protein composition of affinity-purified A028 complexes was nearly identical to that of A complexes formed in the absence of cp028, except A028 no longer contained stoichiometric amounts of the DEAD box protein Prp5 and the splicing factor SPF45, both of which are not involved in B complex formation (Ruby et al., 1993; Lallena et al., 2002; Liang and Cheng, 2015).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies showing Prp5 and SPF45 are not required for B complex formation.

claim: One or more of the B-specific proteins, Lsm proteins, Bact proteins, or Prp19/CDC5L complex proteins may be targeted by cp028.
source: Release of the Lsm proteins and B-specific proteins is blocked, as well as recruitment/stable association of Bact proteins and Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins. Thus, one or more of these proteins may be targetted by cp028, or alternatively the binding partners of these proteins in the B complex may be affected/compromised.
evidence: The manuscript speculates on potential cp028 targets based on B028 composition.

claim: The binding partners of Lsm proteins, B-specific proteins, Bact proteins, or Prp19/CDC5L complex proteins in the B complex may be affected/compromised by cp028.
source: Thus, one or more of these proteins may be targetted by cp028, or alternatively the binding partners of these proteins in the B complex may be affected/compromised.
evidence: The manuscript speculates on an alternative mechanism of cp028 action.

claim: Modified versions of cp028 containing a tag at the ethylphenyl position can be generated and potentially used to identify its target(s) in the spliceosome.
source: Our structure-activity relationship studies revealed chemical groups that do not contribute to the inhibition activity of cp028, such as the primary ethyl group. Thus, modified versions of cp028 containing a tag at this position can be generated and potentially used in future experiments to identify its target(s) in the spliceosome.
evidence: The manuscript proposes future experiments using tagged cp028 analogues.

claim: Small molecule inhibitors of pre-mRNA splicing are important tools for identifying new spliceosome assembly intermediates.
source: Small molecule inhibitors of pre-mRNA splicing are important tools for identifying new spliceosome assembly intermediates, allowing a finer dissection of spliceosome dynamics and function.
evidence: The manuscript states the importance of small molecule inhibitors in the abstract.

claim: U4/U6 snRNP proteins are released during activation before the U6 Lsm and B-specific proteins.
source: Characterization of the stalled complexes (designated B028) revealed that U4/U6 snRNP proteins are released during activation before the U6 Lsm and B-specific proteins, and before recruitment and/or stable incorporation of Prp19/CDC5L complex and other Bact complex proteins.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding in the abstract.

claim: U4/U6 snRNP proteins are released before recruitment and/or stable incorporation of Prp19/CDC5L complex and other Bact complex proteins.
source: Characterization of the stalled complexes (designated B028) revealed that U4/U6 snRNP proteins are released during activation before the U6 Lsm and B-specific proteins, and before recruitment and/or stable incorporation of Prp19/CDC5L complex and other Bact complex proteins.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding in the abstract.

claim: The U2/U6 RNA network in B028 complexes differs from that of the Bact complex.
source: The U2/U6 RNA network in B028 complexes differs from that of the Bact complex, consistent with the idea that the catalytic RNA core forms stepwise during the B to Bact transition and is likely stabilized by the Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding in the abstract.

claim: The catalytic RNA core forms stepwise during the B to Bact transition.
source: The U2/U6 RNA network in B028 complexes differs from that of the Bact complex, consistent with the idea that the catalytic RNA core forms stepwise during the B to Bact transition and is likely stabilized by the Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins.
evidence: The manuscript infers stepwise formation based on B028 RNA structure.

claim: The catalytic RNA core is likely stabilized by the Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins.
source: The U2/U6 RNA network in B028 complexes differs from that of the Bact complex, consistent with the idea that the catalytic RNA core forms stepwise during the B to Bact transition and is likely stabilized by the Prp19/CDC5L complex and related proteins.
evidence: The manuscript infers a stabilization role for Prp19/CDC5L complex based on B028 composition and RNA structure.

claim: The spliceosome is a highly dynamic ribonucleoprotein (RNP) macromolecular complex.
source: The precise excision of an intron from a pre-mRNA and the concomitant ligation of its flanking exons (pre-mRNA splicing) are catalysed by the spliceosome, a highly dynamic ribonucleoprotein (RNP) macromolecular complex.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Spliceosomes assemble de novo on the pre-mRNA substrate in a stepwise manner by the sequential recruitment of five small nuclear ribonucleoprotein particles (snRNPs) and numerous non-snRNP factors.
source: Spliceosomes assemble de novo on the pre-mRNA substrate in a stepwise manner by the sequential recruitment of five small nuclear ribonucleoprotein particles (snRNPs) and numerous non-snRNP factors (reviewed by Will and Lührmann, 2006; Wahl et al., 2009).
evidence: The manuscript cites reviews on spliceosome assembly.

claim: The U1 snRNP binds to the 5' splice site (SS) and the U2 snRNP interacts stably with the branch site (BS) of the pre-mRNA, forming the A complex.
source: Initially, the U1 snRNP binds to the 5' splice site (SS) and the U2 snRNP interacts stably with the branch site (BS) of the pre-mRNA, forming the A complex.
evidence: The manuscript describes A complex formation as established knowledge.

claim: Association of the U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP generates the B complex.
source: Subsequently, association of the U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP generates the B complex that remains catalytically inactive until it undergoes extensive compositional and conformational rearrangements, including the dissociation of U1 and U4, resulting in the formation of the Bact complex.
evidence: The manuscript describes B complex formation as established knowledge.

claim: The B complex remains catalytically inactive until it undergoes extensive compositional and conformational rearrangements, including the dissociation of U1 and U4, resulting in the formation of the Bact complex.
source: Subsequently, association of the U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP generates the B complex that remains catalytically inactive until it undergoes extensive compositional and conformational rearrangements, including the dissociation of U1 and U4, resulting in the formation of the Bact complex.
evidence: The manuscript describes B to Bact transition as established knowledge.

claim: The Bact complex is converted into a catalytically active spliceosome (designated B*) by the action of the RNA helicase Prp2.
source: The latter is converted into a catalytically active spliceosome (designated B*) by the action of the RNA helicase Prp2 (Kim and Lin, 1996).
evidence: The manuscript cites a study on Prp2 function.

claim: The B* complex catalyses the first step of splicing, generating the cleaved 5' exon and intron-3' exon lariat intermediates.
source: The B* complex catalyses the first step of splicing, generating the cleaved 5' exon and intron-3' exon lariat intermediates, and at this stage the spliceosomal C complex is generated.
evidence: The manuscript describes the first catalytic step as established knowledge.

claim: The C complex catalyses the second step of splicing, resulting in the ligation of the 5' and 3' exons and release of the intron in the form of a lariat.
source: After additional RNP rearrangements, the C complex catalyses the second step, resulting in the ligation of the 5' and 3' exons and release of the intron in the form of a lariat.
evidence: The manuscript describes the second catalytic step as established knowledge.

claim: During spliceosome assembly and catalytic activation, the snRNA components of the snRNPs, together with the pre-mRNA, form a highly complex, dynamic RNA-RNA network.
source: During spliceosome assembly and catalytic activation, the snRNA components of the snRNPs, together with the pre-mRNA, form a highly complex, dynamic RNA-RNA network (Staley and Guthrie, 1998).
evidence: The manuscript cites a review on RNA-RNA interactions.

claim: At the A complex stage, the U1 snRNA base pairs with the 5´SS of the pre-mRNA and the U2 snRNA basepairs with the BS.
source: At the A complex stage, the U1 snRNA base pairs with the 5´SS of the pre-mRNA and the U2 snRNA basepairs with the BS.
evidence: The manuscript describes RNA interactions in A complex as established knowledge.

claim: Upon integration of the U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP, the 5' end of U2 snRNA base pairs with the 3' end of U6 snRNA, forming U2/U6 helix II.
source: Upon integration of the U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP, in which the U6 and U4 snRNAs are base paired and form two extended RNA helices (U4/U6 stem I and stem II) (Agafonov et al., 2016; Nguyen et al., 2016; Wan et al., 2016b), the 5' end of U2 snRNA base pairs with the 3' end of U6 snRNA, forming U2/U6 helix II (Madhani and Guthrie, 1992), and stem loop I of U5 snRNA interacts with exon nucleotides near the 5´SS (Newman and Norman, 1992; Wyatt et al., 1992; Sontheimer and Steitz, 1993).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies on U2/U6 helix II formation.

claim: Stem loop I of U5 snRNA interacts with exon nucleotides near the 5´SS.
source: Upon integration of the U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP, in which the U6 and U4 snRNAs are base paired and form two extended RNA helices (U4/U6 stem I and stem II) (Agafonov et al., 2016; Nguyen et al., 2016; Wan et al., 2016b), the 5' end of U2 snRNA base pairs with the 3' end of U6 snRNA, forming U2/U6 helix II (Madhani and Guthrie, 1992), and stem loop I of U5 snRNA interacts with exon nucleotides near the 5´SS (Newman and Norman, 1992; Wyatt et al., 1992; Sontheimer and Steitz, 1993).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies on U5 snRNA interactions.

claim: The U1 snRNA is displaced from the 5´SS of the pre-mRNA by the DEAD-box protein Prp28.
source: The U1 snRNA is displaced from the 5´SS of the pre-mRNA by the DEAD-box protein Prp28 (Staley and Guthrie, 1999), allowing the base pairing interaction between the 5´SS and the conserved ACAGA box sequence of the U6 snRNA (Sawa and Abelson, 1992; Wassarman and Steitz, 1992).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies on Prp28 function.

claim: A key step during the spliceosome activation phase is the unwinding of the U4/U6 helices by the RNA helicase Brr2.
source: A key step during the spliceosome activation phase is the unwinding of the U4/U6 helices by the RNA helicase Brr2 (Laggerbauer et al., 1998; Raghunathan and Guthrie, 1998).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies on Brr2 function.

claim: Unwinding of U4/U6 enables U6 to form short duplexes with U2 (U2/U6 helix Ia and helix Ib), and a catalytically important U6 internal stem loop (U6 ISL).
source: This enables U6 to form short duplexes with U2 (U2/U6 helix Ia and helix Ib), and a catalytically important U6 internal stem loop (that is, the U6 ISL), which together coordinate the metal ions important for splicing catalysis (Fica et al., 2013; Hang et al., 2015; Galej et al., 2016; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies on U2/U6 and U6 ISL formation and function.

claim: The catalytic RNA-RNA network involving U2, U6, and U5 snRNA is comprised of RNA structural elements very similar to the catalytic core of group II self-splicing introns.
source: The catalytic RNA-RNA network involving U2, U6, and U5 snRNA, that is ultimately established in the spliceosome is comprised of RNA structural elements very similar to the catalytic core of group II self-splicing introns (Chan et al., 2012; Fica et al., 2014; Hang et al., 2015; Galej et al., 2016; Rauhut et al., 2016; Wan et al., 2016a; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies on the similarity between spliceosome and group II intron catalytic cores.

claim: After the first catalytic step of the splicing reaction, the spliceosome's catalytic RNA network must be further reorganized to align the step two reactants.
source: After the first catalytic step of the splicing reaction, the spliceosome's catalytic RNA network must be further reorganized to align the step two reactants (Smith and Konarska, 2008; Horowitz, 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies on RNA rearrangements between catalytic steps.

claim: The protein composition of the spliceosome is highly dynamic, with extensive exchanges of proteins occurring from one step to another.
source: The protein composition of the spliceosome is also highly dynamic, with extensive exchanges of proteins occurring from one step to another (Fabrizio et al., 2009; Agafonov et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies on spliceosome protein dynamics.

claim: During the B to Bact transition, about 30 proteins leave the human spliceosome.
source: During the B to Bact transition, about 30 proteins leave the human spliceosome (Bessonov et al., 2010; Agafonov et al., 2011), including the U4/U6-specific and Lsm proteins, and also the B-specific proteins.
evidence: The manuscript cites studies on protein loss during B to Bact transition.

claim: More than 35 proteins are recruited or stably-integrated during Bact formation.
source: More than 35 proteins are recruited or stably-integrated during Bact formation.
evidence: The manuscript states the number of proteins recruited during Bact formation.

claim: The Prp19/CDC5L complex is thought to enter the spliceosome as a pre-assembled complex.
source: These include proteins belonging to the Prp19/CDC5L complex, which is thought to enter the spliceosome as a pre-assembled complex (Makarova et al., 2004; Grote et al., 2010).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies on Prp19/CDC5L complex assembly.

claim: The yeast NTC has been shown to play an essential role in spliceosome activation, with NTC proteins stabilizing the interaction of U5 and U6 with the spliceosome after U4 has been released.
source: The yeast equivalent of the human Prp19/CDC5L complex - the NTC - has been shown to play an essential role in spliceosome activation, with NTC proteins stabilizing the interaction of U5 and U6 with the spliceosome after U4 has been released (Chan et al., 2003).
evidence: The manuscript cites a study on NTC function in yeast.

claim: NTC/NTC-related proteins are in intimate contact with the catalytically active RNA network within the Bact, C and post-catalytic ILS spliceosomes.
source: Furthermore, NTC/NTC-related proteins are in intimate contact with the catalytically active RNA network within the Bact, C and post-catalytic ILS spliceosomes (Yan et al., 2015; Galej et al., 2016; Rauhut et al., 2016; Wan et al., 2016a; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript cites structural studies showing NTC protein-RNA contacts.

claim: Small molecules have proven highly useful to study many cellular processes such as transcription and translation.
source: Small molecules have proven highly useful to study many cellular processes such as transcription and translation, and their potential for dissecting the complex process of pre-mRNA splicing is becoming increasingly clear.
evidence: The manuscript states the utility of small molecules as established knowledge.

claim: Splicing is linked to human diseases, including cancer.
source: Given the link between splicing and human diseases, including cancer (reviewed by Padgett, 2012; Singh and Cooper, 2012; Scotti and Swanson, 2016), small molecules that modulate the splicing process are also potentially of therapeutic value (Bonnal et al., 2012; Ohe and Hagiwara, 2015).
evidence: The manuscript cites reviews on the link between splicing and disease.

claim: Small molecules that modulate the splicing process are potentially of therapeutic value.
source: Given the link between splicing and human diseases, including cancer (reviewed by Padgett, 2012; Singh and Cooper, 2012; Scotti and Swanson, 2016), small molecules that modulate the splicing process are also potentially of therapeutic value (Bonnal et al., 2012; Ohe and Hagiwara, 2015).
evidence: The manuscript cites reviews on the therapeutic potential of splicing modulators.

claim: Spliceostatin A, Pladionelide B, Sudemycin, GEX1A and related compounds target the U2-associated SF3b protein complex and stall splicing during the A complex stage.
source: These include, among others: (i) Spliceostatin A, Pladionelide B, Sudemycin, GEX1A and related compounds that target the U2-associated SF3b protein complex (Kaida et al., 2007; Kotake et al., 2007; Fan et al., 2011; Hasegawa et al., 2011) and stall splicing during the A complex stage (Roybal and Jurica, 2010; Corrionero et al., 2011; Folco et al., 2011), (ii) isoginkgetin (O'Brien et al., 2008) and (iii) 1,4 napthoquinones and 1,4-heterocyclic quinones, which block specifically the second catalytic step of splicing (Berg et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies on various splicing inhibitors.

claim: 1,4 napthoquinones and 1,4-heterocyclic quinones block specifically the second catalytic step of splicing.
source: These include, among others: (i) Spliceostatin A, Pladionelide B, Sudemycin, GEX1A and related compounds that target the U2-associated SF3b protein complex (Kaida et al., 2007; Kotake et al., 2007; Fan et al., 2011; Hasegawa et al., 2011) and stall splicing during the A complex stage (Roybal and Jurica, 2010; Corrionero et al., 2011; Folco et al., 2011), (ii) isoginkgetin (O'Brien et al., 2008) and (iii) 1,4 napthoquinones and 1,4-heterocyclic quinones, which block specifically the second catalytic step of splicing (Berg et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites a study on quinone inhibitors.
